verdict.rationale: Bitwarden markets itself as 'the most trusted open source password manager' and community members explicitly cite open-source clients as the reason they trust it with secrets (bitwarden-probe-1, bitwarden-comm-15). However, the evidence also documents a real controversy where SDK code (used by clients) was briefly relicensed away from a fully open license before being reverted after community pressure, which shows scrutiny worked but also that openness has not always been airtight (bitwarden-comm-1, bitwarden-comm-3, bitwarden-comm-4). Missing for 10: direct links to client-app GitHub repos, explicit confirmation that seed/TOTP-handling code specifically is open and audited, and independent third-party code audits corroborating the open-source claim.
